He required temporary haemodialysis for a month until his condition improved.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man presented with an 18-year history of recurrent aseptic meningitis, accompanied by low-grade fever, general fatigue, arthralgia, urticaria, high fever, and headache. Initial workup showed normal/mildly elevated WBC and CRP during meningitis episodes, CSF with >1000 polymorphonuclear leucocytes/mm3, negative cultures/PCR for infectious agents, and negative genetic analysis for common autoinflammatory conditions (MEFV, MVK, TNFRSF1A, NLRP3, NLRP12). At age 68, the patient developed severe hemolysis, characterized by brownish urine, altered consciousness, hemoglobin of 8.2 g/dL, elevated LDH (3004 IU/L), and acute renal failure (creatinine 2.8 to 8.65 mg/dL) requiring temporary hemodialysis. Flow cytometric analysis confirmed Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) by revealing a deficiency of CD59 and CD55 on erythrocytes and granulocytes. Treatment with eculizumab, an anti-C5 antibody, was initiated immediately after diagnosis. This treatment led to the complete disappearance of urticaria, arthralgia, headache, and hemolysis, with remission lasting 3 years.
